resources.string: Atrial cutaways
Opened atria compared side by side: right atrium on the left, left atrium on the right. These are separate cutaways.
Superior caval opening
The superior vena cava opens high in the right atrium. The inferior vena cava opens below in the same smooth-walled venous region.
Right pectinate ridges
These muscle ridges fan out into the right atrial appendage from the terminal crest, which separates the ridged wall from the smooth venous region.
Fossa ovalis
This shallow oval depression is on the septal wall of the right atrium. It is a remnant of the fetal foramen ovale, not an open passage in this adult view.
Pulmonary vein openings
Four openings are shown in the back of the left atrium, two from each lung. They admit blood returning from the lungs.
Smooth left atrial wall
Most of the left atrial lining is smooth, including the posterior wall between the pulmonary vein openings. Pectinate ridges are confined to the left atrial appendage.
Ventricular short axis
Mid-ventricular cross-section looking from base toward apex: crescent-shaped right cavity at upper left and rounded left cavity at lower right.
Thin right free wall
The outer muscle wall of the right ventricle is thinner than the left. In this section it forms the outer arc of the crescent.
Right ventricular ridges
Coarse muscular ridges, called trabeculae carneae, project into the right ventricular cavity from its inner surface.
Muscular ventricular septum
This shared muscular wall separates the two ventricular cavities and forms the inner arc of the right ventricular crescent.
Thick left free wall
The left ventricular muscle is thicker than the right free wall. It forms most of the ring around the rounded left cavity, completed by the septum.
Four valve faces

Closed valve faces shown separately, not in one plane or at one moment: right heart on the left, left heart on the right; outflow valves above, inlet valves below. Viewed from the arteries or atria, respectively.
Pulmonary cusps
Three pocket-shaped cusps meet at the center of the pulmonary valve, at the exit from the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk.
Aortic cusps
The aortic valve has three semilunar cusps: right coronary, left coronary, and noncoronary. They close together at the exit from the left ventricle into the aorta.
Tricuspid leaflets
The right inlet has three main leaflets: anterior, posterior, and septal. The broad anterior leaflet is usually the largest.
Mitral leaflets
The left inlet has two main leaflets. The deeper anterior leaflet meets the shallower, scalloped posterior leaflet along a curved closure line.
